newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten gets no thanks from HK's last legislature.
newsitem.headline: Patten gets no thanks from HK's last legislature.

text.p: Hong Kong lawmakers snubbed Governor Chris Patten on Wednesday when they voted against a traditional motion to say "thank you" for his last annual state of the colony address.
Sovereignty of the British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997, and Beijing plans to dismantle the elected Legislative Council and replace it with an interim appointed body.
Patten gave his swansong policy speech to the legislature on October 11. In response, the council voted 23 to 22 to scrap the annual motion to express gratitude to the governor.
Patten is famed for introducing democratic reforms in the territory and raising the ire of Beijing.
Opponents from the pro-democracy camp said Patten's reforms did not go far enough, while pro-Beijing legislators attacked his confrontational stand with China.
